 FC Bengaluru United secure first IFL win, beat Mohammedan SC 4-3 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 6 November 2026, 7:02 pm 
 2 min read
 6 Nov 2026 
 FC Bengaluru United clinched their first victory of the Indian Football League (IFL) 2026-27 season by defeating Mohammedan SC 4-3 in a thrilling match at the Bangalore Football Stadium on November 6.
 The match saw FC Bengaluru United take an early two-goal lead within the first 20 minutes through headers by Marat Tareck and Gautam A. Virwani. Mohammedan SC responded when Maharabam Maxion scored in the 26th minute. In the second half, Ngangbam Naocha Singh restored Bengaluru’s two-goal advantage in the 53rd minute, but Mohammedan fought back with goals from Lalthankima five minutes later and Lalremsanga Fanai in the 78th minute, levelling the score at 3-3.

 As the match appeared to be heading towards a draw, substitute Akshunna Tyagi scored a stoppage-time winner in the 91st minute with a header, securing all three points for FC Bengaluru United and marking their first-ever win in the league.
 The home side utilised their familiarity with the conditions to exert pressure early on. Jojo Zaihmingthanga was fouled on the edge of the box, leading to a free-kick by Dhruv Sharma, whose powerful left-footed shot was saved by goalkeeper Nikhil Deka. Jojo later assisted Marat Tareck to open the scoring with a header from a corner. FC Bengaluru United doubled their lead soon after when Gautam A. Virwani scored another header from a Dhruv Sharma corner.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Mohammedan SC responded by creating several chances, with striker Lalremsanga Fanai directing attacks. Following an error by FC Bengaluru United’s captain Abdul Hannan, Yash Chickro’s shot was blocked, but Maharabam Maxion capitalised on the rebound to score. Despite pressure from Bengaluru, goalkeeper Nikhil Deka made several acrobatic saves to keep the deficit at one goal by half-time.
 Early in the second half, FC Bengaluru United almost extended their lead when Chunsaba Bariam’s shot struck the post and was kept out by Deka’s dive. The home team then scored their third goal when right back Ngangbam Naocha Singh headed in a cross from Dhruv Sharma. Mohammedan SC reduced the lead again when Lalthankima scored following Lalremsanga Fanai’s efforts.
 Mohammedan continued their attacks, with Lalremsanga Fanai scoring a well-taken equaliser after a cross from substitute Jeremy Laldinpuia, bringing the score to 3-3. However, FC Bengaluru United secured the victory in stoppage time when Lalramdinsanga Ralte’s corner found substitute Akshunna Tyagi, who scored the winning header.
